text:
maria: Quick check — we're finalizing the async job contract for the new batch transform endpoint. Two open questions: 1) response shape for create (202 vs 200 + job id), and 2) cancel semantics when a job completes during a cancel. Anyone got strong opinions?

kevin: I vote 202 + Location header pointing to /jobs/:job_id and include {job_id} in body. keeps it RESTy and lets clients poll.

ashley: Agree. +1 to including a small status field in the create response like { job_id, status: "queued" } so we avoid the client assuming started.

jonathan: For cancel, I'd prefer idempotent semantics: POST /jobs/:id/cancel returns 202 if cancel requested, 204 if already cancelled, 409 if job already completed successfully. But 409 feels heavy. Maybe always return 200/202 and embed result?

kevin: We should be careful about races. Typical case: client sends cancel, job completes milliseconds later. Server might process cancel after completion. How do we signal that to client?

maria: Proposal: cancel endpoint behavior: - If job terminal (succeeded/failed/cancelled) -> return 409 + body {status: terminal_status} (so client knows outcome). - If cancel accepted -> return 202 + { status: "cancelling" } and schedule best-effort kill. - If job already cancelled -> 204 with no body. Thoughts?

ashley: 409 is ok but clients will have to special-case. Alternative: always return 200 with {accepted: bool, final_status_if_known: string?}. Simpler for client SDKs.

jonathan: I actually like 200 with meta because it compresses cases. Example: {accepted:true, state:"cancelling", final_state:null} or {accepted:false, state:"completed", final_state:"succeeded"} if race.

maria: That mirrors idempotence and avoids throwing HTTP error codes for common races. I can live with 200. We just need to document the race window: server may return final_state when cancellation arrived too late.

deploy-bot: New API PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1492 (draft)

kevin: Also need to pick status schema for GET /jobs/:id. Suggested minimal shape: { job_id, status, created_at, started_at?, finished_at?, result_url?, error? } status enum: queued, running, cancelling, cancelled, failed, succeeded.

ashley: Add metadata: {attempts, worker_id?} optional. And include "progress" (0-100) for long-running jobs. 

maria: Good. And about polling token TTL — we discussed poll tokens for long streaming? For this endpoint we won't issue special poll tokens. Polling is stateless via job_id; token TTL not applicable. For subscription/webhook flows we have ephemeral tokens.

jonathan: One more: back-compat for older clients that expect immediate 200 with result for quick jobs. We should support a query param ?wait=0|n to let client wait up to n seconds synchronously and return 200 with result if completed within wait window. If not, return 202 + job_id as usual.

maria: Love that. Document: POST /batch-transform -> if ?wait=0 (default) immediate 202+job, if ?wait=5 server may block up to 5s and return 200 with result if finished. Clear caveats about tie to request timeouts and proxies.

ashley: Edgecase: client uses wait and then cancels during the blocked wait — cancellation path should be the same (client calls cancel) and server will respond according to race rules.

kevin: Final checklist for spec update: - Create response: 202 + {job_id, status:"queued"} + Location header - Optional ?wait param semantics and 200-with-result fallback - GET /jobs/:id shape with status enum - POST /jobs/:id/cancel -> 200 with {accepted, state, final_state?} - Document race window and guarantee: if cancel accepted before terminal, job will be attempted to stop but may still finish.

maria: I'll update the PR with those exact shapes and add examples. Assigning to @maria to update docs, @devex-bot please generate SDK note once merged. :thumbsup:

devex-bot: Noted — will enqueue SDK changelog entry when PR merges.

ashley: :thumbsup: quick follow-up — can we add a sample cURL snippet in the docs showing ?wait usage? small paste:```bash
# wait up to 3 seconds synchronously
curl -X POST 'https://api.redwood.ai/batch-transform?wait=3' -d '{"input": [...]}' 
```

maria: Perfect. I'll add that and a short section on "handling cancel races" with recommended client behavior: retry GET after cancel to observe final status, don't assume cancellation unless status is cancelled.

kevin: OK. moving to PR review. Thanks all.
